en: If you're nearsighted and you skip your glasses, are you hurting your eyes?
Or giving them a workout that helps?
Take a guess.
I'm Max, and this is Max Wise.
First, let's see how an eye focuses.
Light comes in through the clear front of the eye, the cornea.
Then the lens fine tunes the focus.
In a sharp eye, the picture lands right on the retina at the back.
In most nearsighted eyes, the eyeball has grown a bit too long.
So light comes into focus just in front of the retina.
Faraway things turn blurry.
Here's the key part.
Resting or rubbing your eyes can't shrink that eyeball back.
Real nearsightedness doesn't just wear off.
Lots of people fear that glasses make your eyes weaker.
Eye doctors say that's a myth.
Glasses don't change your eye at all.
The lenses just bend the light, so the picture lands on the retina again.
So for most adults, taking glasses off won't hurt the eye, or heal it.
You simply see less clearly.
But going without often means squinting.
Squinting makes a tiny peephole, so things look sharper for a moment.
Do it all day, and you may end up with tired eyes and headaches.
For kids, there's a bigger risk.
If one eye sees much worse than the other, the brain may start to rely on the better eye.
The blurry one can become a lazy eye.
That's why treating it early really matters.
So follow your eye doctor's plan, especially for children.
And wear them whenever you need to see far away, like when you drive.
Skipping glasses won't heal your eyes, and wearing them won't ruin them.
They just help you see the world clearly.
Stay curious!
